summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin, and medication non-adherence was admitted for abdominal pain, lower extremity swelling, and severe anemia with a hemoglobin of 6.7 g/dL. She had stopped taking her furosemide due to polyuria, leading to fluid retention. Evaluation revealed guaiac-positive stools and a supratherapeutic INR of 3.9. She received two units of packed red blood cells. A CT scan showed diverticulosis without active bleeding, and an EGD revealed no active lesion but signs of esophageal reflux. The bleeding source remained unclear, likely a slow GI bleed. Warfarin was held during admission and planned to be restarted post-discharge. She improved clinically, with hemoglobin rising to 8.3 g/dL, and was discharged home with a rolling walker, home physical therapy, and plans for outpatient capsule endoscopy and hematology follow-up.
problems: Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
